title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. Markets price monopoly margins fast, and punish recurring cost surprises just as fast.
epigraph.author: Institutional Desk Maxim

web_blocks.html: On November 23, 2026, MCX closed at ₹3,581.60 on our exchange ledger (TradingView close: ₹3,565.00) [23]. That sits 5.1% below its ₹3,774.00 52-week high. The price reflects the January 2, 2026 1:5 split across 25.50 crore shares [24]. Market cap stands at ₹91,287.08 crore on TradingView (₹90,945 crore on Screener) [1, 23]. Against ₹3,056 crore TTM sales and ₹1,799 crore TTM PAT (₹70.55 EPS), MCX trades at 50.4x TV TTM P/E (50.6x Screener) and 25.8x book value [1, 23]. High multiples rest on 71.4% ROCE, 56.3% FY26 ROE (64.3% TV TTM), zero debt, and 76% Q2 margins [1, 8, 9, 23].

Pass 1 uncovered three profit frictions that sharpen our model [28, 29, 31]. First, MD & CEO Praveena Rai confirmed higher IT spend is recurring opex, not one-off capex [28, 29]. MCX is nearly doubling system capacity and upgrading cybersecurity. Second, CME Group license fees (~10% of energy revenue; ₹107.96 crore in FY26) scale with crude volume [28, 29]. Third, Q2 effective tax spiked to 28.9% (₹184.67 crore) on an MCXCCL catch-up [31]. Management guided for a ~25% normal tax rate ahead, up from 21.2% in FY26 [28, 29]. CFO Chandresh Shah also noted Q2's zero SGF holiday is temporary [29].

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF: Implied Growth Baked Into MCX's ₹91,287.08 Cr Market Cap (Ledger CMP ₹3,581.60 / TV ₹3,565.00)
rows: Prices in ~28% Y1–Y5 growth fading to ~12% Y6–Y10
Headline FY26 CFO (₹3,035 Cr) includes clearing margin inflows
Reflects ~25% tax, recurring IT opex & CME energy royalties
web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹3,581.60 (50.6x Screener P/E), MCX prices in ~21%–23% annual PAT compounding for a decade. Recurring IT opex, ~25% tax, and CME fees trim our FY28E Base EPS from ₹98 to ₹94.

web_blocks.html: We must separate headline cash flow from owner free cash flow. Screener shows ₹3,035 crore of FY26 operating cash flow [1]. Roughly half came from clearing member margin deposits. Other Liabilities jumped from ₹2,440 crore in FY25 to ₹4,648 crore in FY26 [1]. MCX earns treasury yield on this float—lifting Other Income to ₹170 crore TTM—but cannot pay deposits out to owners [1, 10]. Stripping float leaves normalized owner FCF near PAT (~₹1,450 crore FY26; ~₹1,800 crore TTM). That puts MCX at 50x–52x owner FCF.

web_blocks.caption: Indian Market Infrastructure Peer Comparison (Same-Session Snapshot, 23 Nov 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: MCX leads listed peers with 71.4% ROCE and trades at 50.4x–50.6x P/E—in line with BSE (50.0x, 60.0% ROCE) and below CDSL (58.5x, 32.0% ROCE).

web_blocks.mechanism: IEX held a ~90%+ monopoly in Indian short-term electricity trading with ~50%+ ROCE and traded above 50x–60x P/E at its 2021 peak before CERC/Ministry of Power market-coupling proposals threatened its price-discovery moat.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: IEX de-rated from >60x P/E in 2021 to ~20x P/E despite maintaining >50% ROCE and high operating margins.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even near-100% Indian exchange monopolies can suffer severe multiple compression if the regulator alters fee structures, contract rules, or market-structure exclusivity; never pay full multiples without a margin of safety.

web_blocks.html: Our forward earnings bridge starts from ₹34.04 H1 FY27 EPS [1, 8]. Q2 already absorbed the 28.9% MCXCCL tax catch-up [31]. Strong breadth—₹12.63 lakh crore F&O ADT, ₹10,291 crore options premium ADT, 19.8 lakh H1 clients, Silver 100g, and Electricity Futures—supports ₹76–₹78 FY27E EPS [11, 29, 30]. Modeling ~21% FY28E growth net of ~25% tax, recurring IT opex, CME fees, and SGF resumption yields ₹94.00 FY28E Base EPS (₹2,397 crore PAT) [28, 29, 31]. That trims our prior ₹98.00 estimate by 4.1%.

Applying 44x forward P/E to ₹94.00 EPS yields our refreshed Base Target of ₹4,150.00 (+15.9% vs CMP; +19.9% vs ₹3,460 support top). Our Bull Case is ₹5,000.00 (~45.5x ₹110 EPS) if options premium ADT tops ₹12,000 crore. Our Bear Case is ₹2,350.00 (40x ₹58.75 EPS) if volatility cools—as hinted by silver's 14-month low on November 25, 2026 [35]—or SEBI curbs weekly options. Under severe IEX-style de-rating (25x ₹58.75 EPS), tail risk reaches ₹1,469 (-59.0%).

web_blocks.caption: MCX Forward Valuation Sensitivity Matrix (FY28E EPS vs. Exit P/E Multiple)
web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹3,581.60, MCX prices in ~₹81–₹85 of FY28E EPS at 42x–44x. A de-rating to 36x on ₹94 EPS (₹3,384) leaves negative upside above ₹3,460.

web_blocks.html: Balance-sheet and payout checks confirm the same discipline. On September 30, 2026, MCX held ₹3,106 crore in investments, ₹9 crore in debt, ₹3,512 crore net worth, and ₹1,472.16 crore Core SGF [1, 29]. Deducting ~₹2,000 crore of own cash gives an enterprise value near ₹89,287 crore, or 39.5x TTM EBITDA [1]. Meanwhile, FY26 dividend payout fell to 15% of PAT (₹8.00/share, 0.22% yield), down from 62%–65% in FY20–FY23 [32]. Cash is piling into treasury funds and new ventures like MCX Mineral Exchange. With no yield cushion, entry price discipline is vital.

Valuation Trigger: We would lift our ₹4,150 target toward ₹4,600+ if options premium ADT tops ₹12,000 crore with stable IT opex. We would cut toward ₹2,350 if premium ADT drops below ₹7,500 crore, tax stays above 27%, or SEBI curbs weekly options.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I step out of the price-blind room and look at the refreshed November 23, 2026 tape. MCX closed at ₹3,581.60 on our exchange facts ledger—and ₹3,565.00 on TradingView—pulling back 5.1% from its ₹3,774.00 52-week high. Adjusted for the 1:5 stock split that took effect on January 2, 2026 across 25.50 crore shares, that gives India's dominant commodity exchange a market capitalization of ₹91,287 crore on TradingView and ₹90,945 crore on Screener.

At 50.4x to 50.6x trailing twelve-month earnings and 25.8x book value, MCX has cooled from its mid-November peak near ₹3,730, yet it is still priced as a premier compounder. Over the trailing twelve months, revenue reached ₹3,056 crore and net profit reached ₹1,799 crore, or ₹70.55 per share, backed by 71.4% ROCE, 56.3% audited FY26 ROE (64.3% TTM ROE), and zero debt.

Here is why our Pass 1 forensic refresh matters so much to the valuation model. Previously, investors assumed post-TCS technology costs would sit flat around ₹90 to ₹110 crore a year and that MCX's 21.2% FY26 effective tax rate would hold. On the November 2026 Q2 FY27 earnings call, management corrected both assumptions: higher IT spending is recurring operational opex needed to nearly double exchange capacity and strengthen cybersecurity, CME Group energy license fees scale at roughly 10% of energy contract revenue, and normalized effective tax rates are stepping up toward ~25% after Q2's 28.9% MCXCCL catch-up—while Q2's zero SGF contribution holiday is only temporary.

When we plug those realities into our Reverse DCF at ₹3,581.60—using a 12% discount rate and a 4% terminal growth rate—the market is pricing in roughly 21% to 23% annual earnings compounding over the next decade. That is achievable for a >98%–99% domestic commodity monopoly, especially after GIFT City's IIBX gold volume collapsed to 916.2 kg in FY26, but it leaves thin margin for error.

We also keep our forensic filter on cash flow. Yes, FY26 operating cash flow hit ₹3,035 crore, more than double net profit. Yet roughly half of that inflow came from clearing-member margin deposits sitting inside Other Liabilities, which jumped from ₹2,440 crore to ₹4,648 crore. MCX earns valuable float income on those deposits, but the principal belongs to clearing participants. True normalized owner free cash flow tracks net profit closely (~₹1,450 crore in FY26 and ~₹1,800 crore trailing), placing MCX on 50x to 52x normalized owner FCF.

Against Indian market-infrastructure peers on the same November 23 session, MCX holds its own: BSE trades at 50.0x P/E with 60.0% ROCE, and CDSL trades at 58.5x P/E with 32.0% ROCE. Still, the ghost of Indian Energy Exchange—which de-rated from over 60x to ~20x P/E despite >50% ROCE when regulatory market-coupling risk arrived—reminds us never to overpay for a regulated tollbooth.

Incorporating Pass 1's ~25% normalized tax rate, recurring IT opex, CME royalties, and eventual SGF resumption trims our FY28E Base Case EPS modestly from ₹98 to ₹94 (from ₹76–₹78 in FY27E). Applying a cooler 44x forward multiple yields a refreshed Base Case fair value of ₹4,150. In our Bull Case of ₹110 EPS at ~45.5x, MCX reaches ₹5,000; in our Bear Case of a bullion/energy volatility lull or SEBI fee pressure compressing EPS to ₹58.75 at 40x, it falls to ₹2,350.

Look at what that modest target trim does to the arithmetic: at ₹3,581.60, upside to ₹4,150 is +15.9% against a -15.0% drop to our ratcheted ₹3,043.24 stop—a barely-above-even 1.06-to-1 ratio. Waiting for a 3.4% dip into ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 expands upside to +19.9% and trims stop risk to -12.0%, restoring a 1.66-to-1 institutional setup.

Step back and compare how the market prices MCX across three separate lenses: trailing earnings, normalized owner free cash flow, and enterprise value to operating profit. On trailing earnings, ₹3,581.60 against ₹70.55 of TTM EPS sits just above 50x—virtually identical to BSE at 50.0x and roughly eight turns cheaper than CDSL at 58.5x, even though MCX delivers 71.4% ROCE versus BSE's 60.0% and CDSL's 32.0%. On normalized owner free cash flow—stripping out clearing-member margin deposits that boosted FY26 headline operating cash flow to ₹3,035 crore—MCX trades at 50x to 52x true owner cash generation. And on enterprise value, deducting roughly ₹2,000 crore of unencumbered corporate cash from the ₹91,287 crore market capitalization leaves an enterprise value near ₹89,287 crore, or 39.5x trailing twelve-month EBITDA of ₹2,263 crore.

Why do all three lenses point to the exact same conclusion? Because a 50x exchange multiple only compounds smoothly when both legs of the stool hold steady: first, annual profit growth stays near 20% to 22% as options premium turnover, Silver 100g, and Electricity Futures scale across 19.8 lakh active H1 clients; and second, the regulator leaves weekly options structures and transaction fees undisturbed. Whenever either leg wobbles—as we saw when Q2 effective tax jumped to 28.9% on the MCXCCL catch-up or when silver touched a 14-month low on November 25—paying above ₹3,500 leaves zero valuation shock absorber. Waiting for ₹3,343.80 to ₹3,460.00 buys that exact shock absorber.

book_subsections.title: Why Dividend Payout Compression & Treasury Accumulation Matter
paragraphs: One blind spot our Pass 1 audit surfaced is capital return. Between FY20 and FY23, MCX routinely distributed 62% to 65% of its profits as dividends, and 27% in FY25. In FY26, however, the dividend payout compressed sharply to just 15% of PAT—₹8.00 per post-split share on ₹52.22 EPS—leaving a trailing dividend yield of only 0.22%.

Instead of returning surplus cash, reserves have climbed to ₹3,461 crore and treasury investments sit at ₹3,106 crore, alongside capital earmarked for new subsidiaries like MCX Mineral Exchange (incorporated October 2026). Stripping roughly ₹2,000 crore of unencumbered corporate cash from the ₹91,287 crore market cap leaves an enterprise value near ₹89,287 crore, or 39.5x trailing operating profit.

That capital-allocation shift has a clear implication for valuation: you are not getting paid a cash yield to wait out a quiet commodity quarter. Every rupee of expected return must come from volume-driven EPS compounding and multiple preservation. That is why we refuse to stretch above ₹3,460 for fresh capital.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity Check: Silver's 14-Month Low & Commodity Volatility Regimes
paragraphs: Remember that bullion and energy still account for ~97.6% of MCX's F&O average daily turnover, with gold and silver driving ~66% of H1 FY27 futures volume. When silver dropped to a 14-month low on November 25, 2026, MCX's intraday tape reacted immediately—reminding investors that while volatility boosts trading volume initially, prolonged directional bear markets in precious metals can cool retail options participation.

Look at our sensitivity matrix if volatility cools next year and FY28E EPS lands at ₹72 instead of ₹94. Even at a respectable 40x multiple, the stock would trade at ₹2,880—a 19.6% drawdown from ₹3,581.60. At 36x, it would trade at ₹2,592.

Conversely, buying inside ₹3,343.80–₹3,460.00 lets you pay roughly 36.8x our refreshed ₹94 FY28E Base EPS, protected by a ratcheted ₹3,043.24 stop-loss below the 30-week moving average. That is how you stay disciplined when both the business and the multiple are strong.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Ignore Recurring Opex & Tax Step-Ups
book_callouts.text: A 4-percentage-point jump in normalized tax rate (21.2% to ~25%) plus recurring capacity IT opex does not break a 71%-ROCE monopoly—but it trims fair value by 3% to 5%. Respecting those exact numbers is what keeps you from overpaying at the top of a range.
